title: [MWB] Keyboard does not work on remote machine

judgment.rationale: The report clearly says Mouse Without Borders pairing is far enough along for mouse movement to work, but it still lacks the cross-machine details needed to isolate why only keyboard injection is failing.
evidence: The issue says mouse movement works on the remote machine but typing does not, which narrows the problem to MWB keyboard redirection rather than full pairing failure.
Current source in src/modules/MouseWithoutBorders/App/Class/InputHook.cs and InputSimulation.cs shows separate keyboard-hook capture and simulated input paths.

Current UI text in src/modules/MouseWithoutBorders/App/Form/frmScreen.Designer.cs still exposes a “Reinstall Input hook” recovery action specifically for cases where keyboard or mouse redirection stops working.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask for the failing direction, both-machine elevation state, and fresh diagnostics from both machines so maintainers can tell whether the break is in keyboard capture, transmission, or remote injection.

fix_assessment.rationale: A repository fix may be needed, but the current public evidence does not yet identify whether the failing boundary is the local hook, the network/session path, or remote input injection.

issue_context.summary: The reporter says Mouse Without Borders links far enough for mouse movement to work, but keyboard input never reaches the remote machine.
known_information: The issue is filed against PowerToys 0.100.2 on Windows 11 26200 with a per-user Microsoft Store install.
The reporter already tried rebooting, reconnecting, creating a firewall rule, and resetting one machine.
The local report says PowerToys is running elevated, but it does not describe the other machine’s state.
inferences: This is not a total connectivity failure, because cross-machine mouse movement already works.
The remaining gap could be the keyboard hook, privilege mismatch, or remote SendInput path, and the current issue text does not distinguish among those.
issue_context.analysis: The issue is specific enough to avoid a generic “send logs” response. The source layout shows MWB keyboard redirection crosses several separable boundaries, and the current report only describes the end symptom. The next useful evidence is which direction fails, whether both machines run with matching elevation, and paired diagnostics from both ends of the session.
initial_investigation: src/modules/MouseWithoutBorders/App/Class/InputHook.cs owns the low-level keyboard hook, while src/modules/MouseWithoutBorders/App/Class/InputSimulation.cs performs injected remote input.

src/modules/MouseWithoutBorders/App/Form/frmScreen.Designer.cs includes a tray action labeled “Reinstall Input hook,” which indicates the product already treats stopped input redirection as a distinct failure mode.

information_gaps.information: Which direction fails: local-to-remote only, the reverse direction, or both.
information_gaps.why_needed: This tells maintainers whether the fault is attached to one host session or to the shared pairing state.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reply with the exact machine direction that fails and whether mouse movement still works in that same direction.

information_gaps.information: Whether PowerToys is elevated on both machines and whether either remote target app is elevated when typing fails.
information_gaps.why_needed: Privilege mismatches can block injected keyboard input even when mouse movement is still working.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Confirm for each machine whether PowerToys is running as administrator and whether the failing target window is elevated.

information_gaps.information: Fresh PowerToys diagnostic ZIPs from both machines captured immediately after reproducing the keyboard-only failure.
information_gaps.why_needed: Two-sided diagnostics are the fastest way to see whether the keyboard hook fired locally and whether the remote side accepted or rejected the input path.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reproduce the keyboard failure, then post a comment with /bugreport from each machine immediately afterward.

actions.label: Request MWB keyboard-direction evidence

comment.body:
Thanks for already confirming that the machines link well enough for mouse movement to work. To narrow this to the right Mouse Without Borders keyboard path, please provide:

1. Which direction fails: machine A to B only, B to A only, or both.
2. Whether PowerToys is running as administrator on both machines, and whether the failing target app is elevated.
3. Fresh diagnostics from both machines by reproducing the issue and then posting a comment with /bugreport from each machine immediately afterward.

That will help us tell whether the break is in keyboard capture, transmission, or remote input injection.
